AUTO_SIZE_TEXT_BOX.title: Auto-size text frame set up incorrectly
AUTO_SIZE_TEXT_BOX.why: Frontify grows auto-size frames as people type, and can’t match how these settings resize the frame.
fix: For each frame, open Object > Text Frame Options > Auto-Size and make the change noted next to it.
AUTO_SIZE_TEXT_BOX.subject: frame

EMBEDDED_IMAGE.title: Embedded image
EMBEDDED_IMAGE.why: Frontify needs images as separate linked files and can’t read images embedded in the document.
fix: In Window > Links, select the image and choose Unembed Link from the panel menu.
Save it into the Links folder and package again.
EMBEDDED_IMAGE.subject: image

FILL_TINT.title: Text color tint isn’t 100%
FILL_TINT.why: Frontify shows text colors at full strength, so tinted text will look darker. This check is in beta and can be wrong.
fix: In the paragraph style, go to Character Color and set Tint to 100%.
FILL_TINT.subject: paragraph-style

FONTS_INCLUDED.title: Font missing from the package
FONTS_INCLUDED.why: Frontify needs the font files to render the text, otherwise the template falls back to another font.
fix: Make sure the font is installed or activated on your computer.
Package again with File > Package with "Copy Fonts" checked, and zip the whole folder, including "Document fonts".
FONTS_INCLUDED.subject: font

GRID_ALIGNMENT.title: Text aligned to the baseline grid
GRID_ALIGNMENT.why: Frontify doesn’t use InDesign’s baseline grid, so line spacing will change.
fix: In the paragraph style, go to Indents and Spacing and set Align to Grid to None.
GRID_ALIGNMENT.subject: paragraph-style

IMAGE_INCLUDED.title: Linked image missing from the package
IMAGE_INCLUDED.why: The document links to an image that isn’t in the package, so Frontify can’t show it.
fix: Relink any missing images in Window > Links.
Package again with File > Package with "Copy Linked Graphics" checked.
IMAGE_INCLUDED.subject: image

IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION.title: Image is flipped or skewed
IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION.why: Frontify can’t reproduce flipped or skewed images, so they’ll look different or break when edited.
fix: Select the image and choose Object > Transform > Clear Transformations (or set the shear angle to 0° and remove the flip).
If you need the flipped look, save a flipped copy of the image file instead.
IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION.subject: image

IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION_CONTAINER.title: Image frame is flipped or skewed
IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION_CONTAINER.why: Frontify can’t reproduce flipped or skewed frames, so the image will look different or break when edited.
fix: Select the image frame and choose Object > Transform > Clear Transformations (or set the shear angle to 0° and remove the flip).
IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION_CONTAINER.subject: image

IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION_IMAGE.title: Image is flipped or skewed
IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION_IMAGE.why: Frontify can’t reproduce flipped or skewed images, so they’ll look different or break when edited.
fix: Double-click to select the image inside the frame, then choose Object > Transform > Clear Transformations (or set the shear angle to 0° and remove the flip).
If you need the flipped look, save a flipped copy of the image file instead.
IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION_IMAGE.subject: image

KERNING.title: Kerning isn’t set to Metrics
KERNING.why: Frontify spaces letters using the font’s own kerning (Metrics). Other settings make text shift when it’s edited.
fix: In the paragraph style, go to Basic Character Formats and set Kerning to Metrics.
KERNING.subject: paragraph-style

KERNING_CHAR.title: Kerning isn’t set to Metrics
KERNING_CHAR.why: Frontify spaces letters using the font’s own kerning (Metrics). Other settings make text shift when it’s edited.
fix: In the character style, go to Basic Character Formats and set Kerning to Metrics.
KERNING_CHAR.subject: character-style

LINKED_TEXT_FRAME.title: Threaded (linked) text frames
LINKED_TEXT_FRAME.why: Frontify doesn’t support text flowing from one frame into another.
fix: Turn on View > Extras > Show Text Threads, then double-click a frame’s out port to break the thread so each frame holds its own text.
LINKED_TEXT_FRAME.subject: frame

MASTERPAGE.title: Items on a master page
MASTERPAGE.why: Frontify only reads items on the document pages, so anything on a master page (called a parent page in newer InDesign versions) is ignored or breaks the template.
fix: In the Pages panel, open the master (parent) page and move its items onto the document pages, or delete them.
MASTERPAGE.subject: document

OBJECT_STYLE_IMAGE.title: Object style on an image frame
OBJECT_STYLE_IMAGE.why: Frontify doesn’t apply object styles, so the frame will look different.
fix: Select the frame and apply [None] or [Basic Graphics Frame] in Window > Styles > Object Styles, then re-apply any formatting you need directly.
OBJECT_STYLE_IMAGE.subject: image

OBJECT_STYLE_TEXT.title: Object style on a text frame
OBJECT_STYLE_TEXT.why: Frontify doesn’t apply object styles, so the frame will look different.
fix: Select the frame and apply [None] or [Basic Text Frame] in Window > Styles > Object Styles, then re-apply any formatting you need directly.
OBJECT_STYLE_TEXT.subject: frame

OTF_TTF_FONT.title: Unsupported font format
OTF_TTF_FONT.why: Frontify can only use OpenType (.otf) and TrueType (.ttf) fonts. Other formats, such as Type 1, can’t be loaded.
fix: Get an OTF or TTF version from the font vendor and swap it in with Type > Find/Replace Font.
OTF_TTF_FONT.subject: font

PAGE_ITEM_TRANSFORMATION.title: Item is flipped or skewed
PAGE_ITEM_TRANSFORMATION.why: Frontify can’t reproduce flipped or skewed items, so they’ll look different from the InDesign file.
fix: Select the item and choose Object > Transform > Clear Transformations (or set the shear angle to 0° and remove the flip).
PAGE_ITEM_TRANSFORMATION.subject: frame

PARAGRAPH_STYLE.title: Text without a paragraph style
PARAGRAPH_STYLE.why: Frontify uses paragraph styles to format text and decide what can be edited. Text set to [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style] has nothing to follow.
fix: Select the text and apply a paragraph style in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles (any style except [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style]).
PARAGRAPH_STYLE.subject: frame

PARAGRAPH_STYLE_TEXT_BOX.title: Text frame has no paragraph style
PARAGRAPH_STYLE_TEXT_BOX.why: Frontify uses paragraph styles to format text and decide what can be edited. This frame only uses the default style.
fix: Select the frame and apply a paragraph style in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles (any style except [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style]).
PARAGRAPH_STYLE_TEXT_BOX.subject: frame

PASTED_GRAPHICS.title: Pasted graphic
PASTED_GRAPHICS.why: Graphics pasted straight into InDesign aren’t linked files, so Frontify can’t read them.
fix: Save the graphic as a file (for example SVG, PDF or PNG), delete the pasted version and place the file with File > Place.
PASTED_GRAPHICS.subject: document

TABLE.title: Table in a text frame
fix: Click into the table and choose Table > Convert Table to Text, or rebuild it with separate text frames.
TABLE.subject: frame

TEXT_COLUMNS.title: Text frame has columns
TEXT_COLUMNS.why: Frontify doesn’t support multiple columns inside one text frame.
fix: Set Columns to 1 in Object > Text Frame Options. Use separate text frames if you need columns.
TEXT_COLUMNS.subject: frame

TEXT_WRAP.title: Text wrap applied
TEXT_WRAP.why: Frontify doesn’t support text wrap, so text won’t flow around objects.
fix: Select the frame and choose No Text Wrap in Window > Text Wrap.
TEXT_WRAP.subject: frame

VARIABLE_FONT.title: Variable font used
VARIABLE_FONT.why: Frontify doesn’t support variable fonts, so text using them won’t render correctly.
fix: Install the static (non-variable) version of the font and swap it in with Type > Find/Replace Font.
VARIABLE_FONT.subject: font

EMPTY_TEXT_FRAME.title: Empty text frame
EMPTY_TEXT_FRAME.why: Empty frames are allowed, but are often left over by accident.
fix: Delete the frame if it isn’t needed.
EMPTY_TEXT_FRAME.subject: frame

LARGE_IMAGE.title: Large image
LARGE_IMAGE.why: Very large images slow down editing and exporting in Frontify.
fix: Reduce the image’s pixel size or file size if it doesn’t need to be this large.
LARGE_IMAGE.subject: image

COMPOSER.title: Paragraph Composer used
COMPOSER.why: The Adobe Paragraph Composer breaks lines differently from browsers, so text may reflow in Frontify.
fix: In the paragraph style, go to Justification and set Composer to Adobe Single-line Composer.
COMPOSER.subject: paragraph-style

DOCUMENT_BLEED.title: Document has bleed
DOCUMENT_BLEED.why: Bleed is added to every export, which is right for print templates but usually unwanted for digital ones.
fix: For a digital template, set bleed to 0 in File > Document Setup > Bleed and Slug. For print templates, bleed is fine.
DOCUMENT_BLEED.subject: document

HYPHENATION.title: Hyphenation is on
HYPHENATION.why: Browsers hyphenate differently from InDesign, so lines may break in different places.
fix: In the paragraph style, go to Hyphenation and uncheck Hyphenate.
HYPHENATION.subject: paragraph-style

IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION.title: Image is rotated
IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION.why: Rotation works, but the image may look slightly different in Frontify than in InDesign.
fix: Check the result in Frontify. If it looks off, save a rotated copy of the image and place it unrotated.
IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION.subject: image

IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION_CONTAINER.title: Image frame is rotated
IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION_CONTAINER.why: Rotation works, but the frame may look slightly different in Frontify than in InDesign.
fix: Check the result in Frontify. If it looks off, remove the rotation from the frame.
IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION_CONTAINER.subject: image

IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION_IMAGE.title: Image is rotated
IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION_IMAGE.why: Rotation works, but the image may look slightly different in Frontify than in InDesign.
fix: Check the result in Frontify. If it looks off, save a rotated copy of the image and place it unrotated.
IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION_IMAGE.subject: image

OVERRIDE.title: Text formatted outside its paragraph style
OVERRIDE.why: Formatting added by hand on top of a paragraph style (shown as a + next to the style name) may be lost or look different in Frontify.
fix: Click into the text. A + after the style name in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles means it has extra formatting.
To remove it, select the text and click Clear Overrides at the bottom of the Paragraph Styles panel.
To keep the look, update the style to match instead (right-click the style > Redefine Style), or use a character style for single words.
OVERRIDE.subject: frame

PAGE_ITEM_TRANSFORMATION.title: Item is rotated
PAGE_ITEM_TRANSFORMATION.why: Rotation works, but the item may look slightly different in Frontify than in InDesign.
fix: Check the result in Frontify. If it looks off, remove the rotation.
PAGE_ITEM_TRANSFORMATION.subject: frame

UNUSED_IMAGE.title: Unused images in the package
UNUSED_IMAGE.why: These files aren’t used in the document and only make the package bigger.
fix: Delete the unused files from the Links folder before zipping the package.
UNUSED_IMAGE.subject: image

customer_summary.html:
We checked “Flyer-Sales_Bad” and found 2 issues in the InDesign file that are likely causing the problems in Frontify, plus 3 that may change how it looks. Here’s what to change:

Likely causing the problems

1. Text frame has no paragraph style
Frontify uses paragraph styles to format text and decide what can be edited.
Where: text frames “SuperSale”, “50% off on all products onmonobr…”, “only this weekend” (page 1)

  • Select the frame and apply a paragraph style in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles (any style except [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style]).

Learn more

2. Font missing from the package
Frontify needs the font files to render the text, otherwise the template falls back to another font.
Where: the font “Minion Pro”

  • Make sure the font is installed or activated on your computer.
  • Package again with File > Package with "Copy Fonts" checked, and zip the whole folder, including "Document fonts".

Learn more

May change how it looks

3. Text formatted outside its paragraph style
Formatting added by hand on top of a paragraph style (shown as a + next to the style name) may be lost or look different in Frontify.
Where: text frames “SuperSale” (page 1, font, size and leading changed), “50% off on all products onmonobr…” (page 1, font, size and tracking changed), “only this weekend” (page 1, font, size, tracking and more changed)

  • Click into the text. A + after the style name in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles means it has extra formatting.
  • To remove it, select the text and click Clear Overrides at the bottom of the Paragraph Styles panel.
  • To keep the look, update the style to match instead (right-click the style > Redefine Style), or use a character style for single words.

Learn more

4. Document has bleed
Bleed is added to every export, which is right for print templates but usually unwanted for digital ones.
Current bleed: 3 mm on all sides

  • For a digital template, set bleed to 0 in File > Document Setup > Bleed and Slug. For print templates, bleed is fine.

Learn more

5. Paragraph Composer used
The Adobe Paragraph Composer breaks lines differently from browsers, so text may reflow in Frontify.
Where: the paragraph style “[Basic Paragraph]”, used on page 1

  • In the paragraph style, go to Justification and set Composer to Adobe Single-line Composer.

Learn more

Once that’s done, package the document again with File > Package, zip the package folder and upload it to Frontify.
